explanation: The vulnerable code unconditionally calls ssh_no_host_key_check(), which writes a persistent ~/.ssh/config with 'Host * / StrictHostKeyChecking no', disabling SSH host authenticity verification (CWE-295) for the invoking user beyond the lifetime of the kas process and enabling MITM attacks on future SSH connections. The fix gates this behind ctx.managed_env so host key checking is only disabled in externally managed (e.g., CI) environments, materially correcting the defect. This is a real cryptographic-verification misuse fix, consistent with the GHSA advisory, and matches CRYPTO-010 in the target taxonomy.
finding: kas/libcmds.py: execute() unconditionally disables SSH host key checking via ssh_no_host_key_check(), persistently weakening host authenticity verification (CWE-295); fix restricts it to managed environments.
note: The ssh_no_host_key_check() implementation itself is not shown, so the persistent config write is inferred from the advisory details and the fix comment; the shown diff only demonstrates the gating change.
